comparisons.peer_summary: Average loans increased $4.4 billion to $223.9 billion, primarily driven by custom lending and residential mortgage loans, while average deposits decreased $10.8 billion to $287.5 billion due to clients moving deposits to higher yielding investment cash alternatives.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Bank of America provide a segmented breakdown of deposit performance drivers in 2024. Citi reports that its Services segment deposits grew 4% YoY due to transaction banking services (TTS) and securities services growth, whereas BAC reports overall average deposits decreased by $10.8 billion due to client migration to higher-yielding alternatives. Citi's US Personal Banking (USPB) declined 18% due to transfers to Wealth, while BAC does not disclose segment-level deposit growth but notes a broad decline in deposits driven by investment cash alternatives.

sentences.text: • Services increased 4% year-over-year, as TTS increased 3% due to deepened client relationships and growth in operational deposits, and Securities Services increased 11% driven by AUC growth.
• USPB decreased 18% year-over-year, as the transfer of certain relationships and the associated deposits to Wealth more than offset underlying deposit growth.

Average deposits decreased $10.8 billion to $287.5 billion primarily driven by clients moving deposits to higher yielding investment cash alternatives, including offerings on our investment and brokerage platforms.

comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures analyze deposit changes as a component of balance sheet liabilities. Citi details average deposit changes by segment, noting that Services deposits increased 11% due to Asset Under Custody (AUC) growth. Goldman Sachs reports total liabilities increased by $29.29 billion, primarily driven by a $4.60 billion increase in deposits, which it attributes to consumer deposit growth partially offset by decreases in transaction banking deposits.

sentences.text: • Services increased 4% year-over-year, as TTS increased 3% due to deepened client relationships and growth in operational deposits, and Securities Services increased 11% driven by AUC growth.

As of December 2024, total liabilities in our consolidated balance sheets were $1.55 trillion, an increase of $29.29 billion from December 2023, primarily reflecting increases in collateralized financings of $35.03 billion (reflecting the impact of our and our clients' activities), and deposits of $4.60 billion (due to an increase in consumer deposits, partially offset by decreases in transaction banking deposits and other deposits), partially offset by decreases in customer and other payables of $7.47 billion (primarily reflecting our clients' activities) and borrowings of $5.48 billion (driven by net maturities).

comparisons.peer_topic: Deposit balance trends and drivers for 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: Average deposits increased in 2024 compared to 2023 due to growth in CIB (driven by Payments and structured notes) and AWM (higher-yielding products offset by migration), while CCB declined due to increased spending; period-end deposits similarly rose in CIB and AWM but fell in CCB.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and JPMorgan provide segmented analysis of average deposit performance in 2024. Citi reports Services deposits increased 4% YoY, driven by operational deposits, while JPMorgan reports Commercial & Investment Bank (CIB) average deposits increased due to Payments and structured notes. Conversely, Citi reports USPB deposits declined 18% due to transfers to Wealth, while JPMorgan reports Consumer & Community Banking (CCB) average deposits declined due to increased customer spending.

sentences.text: • Services increased 4% year-over-year, as TTS increased 3% due to deepened client relationships and growth in operational deposits, and Securities Services increased 11% driven by AUC growth.
• USPB decreased 18% year-over-year, as the transfer of certain relationships and the associated deposits to Wealth more than offset underlying deposit growth.
Average deposits increased for the year ended December 31, 2024 compared to the year ended December 31, 2023, reflecting:

• an increase in CIB due to net inflows predominantly in Payments and net issuances of structured notes as a result of client demand in Markets, partially offset by deposit attrition, which included actions taken to reduce certain deposits,
• a decline in CCB primarily driven by a decrease in balances in existing accounts due to increased customer spending, largely offset by new accounts.

comparisons.peer_summary: Time deposits are predominantly brokered certificates of deposit, while total deposits in 2024 increased due to higher Savings and Time deposits, offset by reductions in Brokerage sweep deposits driven by client outflows to alternative products.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures discuss the movement of client deposits toward alternative investments or higher-yielding products. Citi notes that its Wealth segment deposits increased 3% but were partially offset by a shift in deposits to higher-yielding investments. Morgan Stanley reports that total deposits increased in 2024 but were partially offset by a reduction in Brokerage sweep deposits due to net outflows to alternative cash equivalent and other investment products.
